newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae to move quickly on new board.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae to move quickly on new board.

text.p: The Student Loan Marketing Association will propose that a dissident shareholder group be represented on its board in order to appeal to the "broadest group" of shareholders, Sallie Mae general counsel Tim Greene said on Tuesday.
A slate to be proposed by Sallie Mae will include "meaningful representation" for the Committee to Restore Value (CRV), a shareholder group that opposes Sallie Mae management, Greene told Reuters.

"The board is considering the makeup of the slate in response to shareholder issues that have been raised," Greene told Reuters. "It is envisioned that there will be a representation for the CRV," he added.
Earlier on Tuesday, Sallie Mae and CRV said they have agreed to hold a joint special meeting at which shareholders will vote on a single privatization and reorganization plan.
They also agreed to nominate separate slates for the 15-member board of directors, which shareholders will choose between at the meeting.
Greene said the Sallie Mae slate would provide meaningful representation for the CRV while maintaining the current management direction.
He declined to say how many CRV representatives Sallie Mae would propose on the 15-member slate. But he said the solution was one designed to "appeal to the broadest group of owners of the company."
Greene said Sallie Mae and CRV had agreed to file a joint, amended S-4 registration statement with their proposals for review by the Securities and Exchange Commission within 10 days.
"We want to get this in front of the shareholders as soon as is practicable," he added.
The special meeting would be held about 20 days after SEC review, he said.
